record.context_brief: Worst-case normalized discrepancy of sign matrices
record.original_question: Let disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity for A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}. What is the exact value of sup_{n in N} sup_{A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}} (1/sqrt(n)) * disc(A)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 (How many deviations are needed afterall?). What is the value of the following quantity? sup_{n∈N} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} (1/√n) disc(A).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$ and a matrix $A \in \{+1,-1\}^{n \times n}$, define the discrepancy
$$\operatorname{disc}(A) \;=\; \inf_{x \in \{+1,-1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ denotes the maximum absolute coordinate. Determine the exact value of
$$C \;=\; \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \; \sup_{A \in \{+1,-1\}^{n \times n}} \frac{\operatorname{disc}(A)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The quantity is bounded above by Spencer's "six standard deviations suffice" theorem (1985), which yields $\operatorname{disc}(A) \le 6\sqrt{n}$ for $\pm 1$ matrices, and matching lower bounds from random matrices show $C$ is a positive constant. However, the exact value of the supremum is not known; determining the optimal constant in Spencer's theorem is a long-standing open problem in discrepancy theory.

status_evidence.title: Six standard deviations suffice
status_evidence.snippet: Spencer (1985) achieves disc(A) ≤ 6√n for ±1 n×n matrices; combined with the random-matrix lower bound this is tight up to a constant.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound 6√n is known; the exact constant is not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Discrepancy Theory Lecture Notes (Nikolov, Prague Summer School 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Spencer's theorem and the still-unknown optimal constant for the worst-case discrepancy of ±1 matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The exact optimal constant remains open.
